title: Accessibility audit of restaurant page
persona: Aditya, designer on Swiggy's discovery surface
scenario: Swiggy's restaurant detail page works fine for most users, but a low-vision tester on contract told eng the menu list is unreadable on her screen-reader and the ‘add’ buttons announce as ‘button button button’. You owe an audit by Wednesday: WCAG 2.2 issues, severity, and which fixes are 1-day vs 1-month effort. You have screenshots, not code access.
badPrompt: do an accessibility audit of swiggy restaurant page
badOutput: Accessibility issues commonly include low contrast, missing alt text, small touch targets, and unclear focus states. You should improve color contrast, add ARIA labels, and ensure keyboard navigation works.

hints.title: Anchor the standard explicitly
hints.body: Say ‘WCAG 2.2 AA’, not just ‘accessibility’. The standard changes what counts as a violation.

hints.title: Force severity + effort
hints.body: Demand each issue ranked by severity AND tagged 1-day vs 1-month effort. Without this, the audit is unprioritised.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, an audit, not generic feedback.
Anchor accessibility specifics, WCAG, ARIA, screen-readers.
Reference the actual user feedback, low-vision tester said the menu is unreadable.
Anchor the surface, restaurant detail page, not the whole app.
Specify the standard, WCAG 2.2 AA, not just ‘accessibility’.
Acknowledge the constraint, audit from screenshots, no code access.
Demand severity ranking, P0/P1/P2 or critical/high/low.
Force effort tagging, 1-day vs 1-month. That's how design and eng prioritise.
Specify a table, issue + WCAG criterion + severity + effort + fix.
Demand the WCAG criterion reference, e.g., 1.4.3, on each issue.

tipIfLow: ‘Do an accessibility audit’ produces generic checklists. The unlock is anchoring the standard (WCAG 2.2 AA), the surface (restaurant page), the user feedback (low-vision tester's quote), AND demanding severity + effort tagging on every issue.
goldPrompt: Act as a senior accessibility consultant. I'm Aditya, designer on Swiggy's discovery surface. A low-vision tester reported the restaurant detail page menu is unreadable on her screen reader and 'add' buttons announce as 'button button button'. Audit against WCAG 2.2 AA. I have screenshots, no code. Output a table: issue, WCAG criterion violated, severity (P0/P1/P2), effort (1-day vs 1-month), recommended fix. Anchor at least 3 issues to her actual feedback. Refuse to invent code-level fixes; describe behaviour and let eng implement.
